description:
## Goal

Expose one authoritative, allocation-conscious telemetry vocabulary for
change-driven work in both compiler2 reactive engines: scheduler jobs/facts and
ProductMemo products.

This ticket observes the current model; it does not add a fixpoint, group, epoch,
cache, or second dependency ledger.

## The seam is the completion event, NOT the job span

The raw job span carries Job, World and JobCompletion -- and covers only 2 of the
5 sites that complete jobs. Measured: 0 `BuildBackendProduct` job spans in a real
public log against 3 `backend_program.defined` events; those completions are
span-less.

    drive.rs:452              span YES
    product_drive.rs:185      span YES
    compiler.rs:139           span NO
    jobs/native.rs:65         span NO
    jobs/macro_runtime.rs:65  span NO

All five route through `ExecutionContext::complete_job` (`drive.rs:29`), which
unconditionally emits `fz.compiler2.work_graph.applied` with
`(&World, &JobCompletion)` (`drive.rs:41`). Verified exhaustively: no caller
reaches `World::complete_job` directly. That event is complete and is simply not
allowlisted (`jsonl.rs:797`).

Project onto it. Leave the job span for timing. Projecting onto the span instead
would leave three completion sites' fact movements invisible, and any formula
later woken by one of them would appear to have no moved input -- silently
falsifying this ticket's own acceptance assertion.

## Verified gap

Scheduler state already knows FactChange, FactMovement, enqueued/coalesced
readers, blocked waits, and rebase state. ProductMemo already knows ProductKey,
generations, dependencies, displacement, and group membership.

The JSONL projection discards the deciding identities:

- Job is serialized as kind only (`jsonl.rs:1081`);
- `AppliedStep.changed` serializes as a count, not changed FactKeys
  (`jsonl.rs:1251`);
- `AppliedStep.movements` is computed (`scheduler.rs:362`) and never projected;
- wake events do not retain the exact FactUse/revision movement that caused an
  agenda entry -- `enqueue_dependents` (`scheduler.rs:395`) holds both `fact_use`
  and the `shift` classification and drops them into a bare `Vec<J>`;
- `write_activation_key` (`jsonl.rs:1462`) emits root_id + function_id and DROPS
  the arrow;
- ProductKey is serialized as kind only (`jsonl.rs:1298`);
- product settlement is under-reported: `finish_group` and `publish_product`
  settle silently, so the log shows 3 `runtime_demand` settlements where >=237
  products settled.

Consequently the public log cannot group 1,382 AnalyzeActivation evaluations by
activation, distinguish distinct product population from re-settlement, or prove
that each evaluation had new input evidence.

## Causality is DERIVED, not stored

`DependencyIndex.reads` is `HashMap<J, HashSet<FactUse<F>>>` (`deps.rs:15`):
which facts a job read, never at what revision. `ProductDependencies`
(`pull.rs:259`) is the opposite -- it stores FactState and generations.

So "did this formula's input move since its own prior conclusion?" cannot be
answered by asking the scheduler without adding the second dependency ledger this
ticket forbids. It IS answerable by replaying the ordered stream: for evaluation
e of formula F, the moved inputs are exactly

    (F's reads UNION F's blocked-set from its previous completion)
      for which a movement appears between F's previous conclusion and e

Reads alone are insufficient: `reads` and `waits` are separate maps
(`deps.rs:15-19`), and a job re-run because a WAIT became satisfiable
(`scheduler.rs:413`) has that fact in `waits`, so a reads-only rule false-flags
it as uncaused.

The one thing that must be CARRIED rather than derived is the wake cause:
enqueued-vs-coalesced is agenda state no fact movement can reconstruct. That is
this ticket's sanctioned exception -- carry the minimal typed cause with the
agenda entry; do not build a telemetry-only graph.

## Within-run identity and cross-run comparison are different requirements

- WITHIN a run, grouping needs only ids that are stable in-process. A raw `Ty`
  id qualifies: free, no rendering, no Types lookup.
- ACROSS runs, raw `Ty` ids are measured unstable (four processes, 16 differing
  arena slots; see fz-kdt.47 and fz-kdt.48), so they cannot be the comparand.

And `Types::display` must NOT be used as the cross-run comparand: it is measured
non-injective -- `Ty(83)` and `Ty(253)` both render `([int]) -> r0` while
`253 <: 83`. Two different activations would compare equal and the acceptance
assertion would pass on genuinely divergent work.

Cross-run equality therefore needs fz-f98.21's faithful canonical form, which
blocks .34.6 only. Chasing structural determinism instead is unbounded work; see
f98.21.

## Output contract

From the public production log alone, an analysis can determine:

- stable formula identity for Job and ProductKey without relying on raw Ty ids;
- initial demand versus exact FactUse/ProductKey generation movement causing
  evaluation;
- old and new dependency state;
- rebased, blocked, concluded, enqueued, or coalesced status;
- exact changed output FactKeys/ProductKeys, not only counts;
- downstream readers woken by each movement;
- product cache hit, reproduction, displacement, and recursive-group membership;
- work-start reason and exact demanded fact/product.

Use the dependency engines' authoritative state. Raw identities flow through
telemetry and are projected only by enabled sinks. Telemetry-disabled runs must
not format types, clone inventories, or query World.

## Decomposition

    .34.1 public-log capture harness
       └─ .34.2 identity in the log (within-run; raw ids, no rendering)
            ├─ .34.3 job causality (Wake + work_graph.applied)
            ├─ .34.4 per-member product settlement
            └─ .34.5 work-start attribution
                 └─ .34.6 acceptance + cross-run equality  [also blocked by fz-f98.21]

.34.1 comes first, not last: every later child asserts against the public log,
and no content-capture helper exists today, so an identity-first ordering would
leave .34.2 unable to write its own red test.

## Acceptance

For enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, and enum_predicate_search,
the public log yields distinct formula/product identities, evaluations per
identity, exact moved-input causes, changed/unchanged outputs, downstream wakes,
blocked and rebased completions, and recursive-group membership.

Every non-initial evaluation must name a dependency whose content/generation
moved since that formula's own prior conclusion. Readiness-only movement is
reported separately. Repeated runs produce identical causal work multisets.
Existing unsanctioned_work_starts==0 and root_scans==0 remain green.

Baseline measured at HEAD (release, 00420_enum_take_drop_split):
17,574 public events; 2,593 job spans; 1,382 AnalyzeActivation; work starts
ignition 2 / changed_revision_wake 1433 / standing_root_frontier 3 /
activation_frontier 282 / blocked_waiter_expansion 873; demand cones 8
settlements at members 1,1,197x4,237x2 with external_members 0 and 6,544
derivations; telemetry on-vs-off wall time indistinguishable.

## Documentation

Update telemetry and performance-instrumentation docs with the causal fields and
machine-independent assertions. Remove descriptions that tell investigators to
infer identity or causality from counts. Docs travel with each child, not
deferred to the last.
title: Expose formula identity and revision causality for scheduler and product work
